title: Mark independent writing live
statement: While learners write on their own, mark their writing live in small, frequent touches, such as a word to swap, so they improve the text as they go.
detail: A planning meeting for a Grade 9 course proposed live marking during independent practice as an effective secondary-school practice: learners write on their own while live marking moments suggest a word to swap, because, as the meeting put it, feedback is most effective little and often and in real time. The course's lesson specification then gave the guide the job of building sentence stems and giving live feedback that moves the learner toward the answer one step at a time. The meeting cited no study for the claim.
against: The same specification says the guide will never "Appear constantly or interrupt unprompted." (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 181), so live feedback has to come without unprompted interruption.

evidence.quote: So, one of the like a really effective practice um particularly in secondary schools is where you get kids just on their own writing, but there are like live marking moments where you know this word or swap out this word and they can be like making notes to just improve that text in real time because feedback is most effective when it's little and often um and in real time.
